It all depends why you are at that particular weight in the first instance.

If you're over or underweight because of an impulse control disorder, or an under/over active metabolism then I would hazard it would be harder to achieve, than say someone who just decided they needed to shed or put on a few pounds.

As for which is harder, each would pose unique challenges, so who dafuq knows.

Gaining. Losing really only requires you eat less(moving more will speed that up). But gaining you not only have to eat more you have to workout so as to not get fat. And the extra food is more expensive as well. But that's just my opinion. Hard thing to quantify really.
If you have a really fast metabolism combined with food allergies gaining mass can be a nightmare. Losing weight however, anyone can do. Just eat less.

Just from my experience in the gym for every ten fat people that show up only three out four skinny people show up. Out of those maybe one from each group will stick it out. From those the fatties will reach their goal weight in almost half the time of the skinnies.

Gaining. Sure, you may think "Oh man, gaining weight. I'll just eat 50 twinkies and I'll be done." Nah, son. That's not what its all about. Let's assume you ate those twinkies every day. You start feeling sluggish and lazy, your teeth feel weak, and you just want to be able to do stuff without getting a headache.

"Alright, so I'll eat a shitload of healthy food until my caloric intake outweighs the calories I burn". Sure, you will still gain fat, but your stomach will hate you forever for always being so full. Plus, since all you're gaining is fat it could possibly just burn off and go away. Not to mention the fact you're probably overloading on macros and micros.

"Alright, so I'll bulk up on healthy food and then I'll burn off the fat to gain muscle and that will make me gain weight!" Bingo. Have fun eating a shitload of food and then working out harder than the average dietgoer just to gain a few pounds.
It depends how large you are. If you are very large, losing 15 kg will be easier. If you are very skinny, gaining 15 kg will be easier.

In the past year I went through both a cutting and a bulking phase. They're both equally difficult to me. The difficulty mainly comes from wanting the change to happen fast -- fast changes are hard, and from wanting to gain without eating junk(chips, deep fried food, cake, etc...)

On a weight gain diet I have to eat almost constantly throughout the day -- every 2-3 hours. It becomes a very annoying chore after a while.
